summary_plain: Moves about 29 arcseconds per hour across 17 images over 36.0 hours. It matches the known asteroid 5193 Tanakawataru (1992 ET).

orbit.reported_orbit: The arc is too short to fix one orbit, so this is the most circular of the 422 sampled orbits that fit the detections; the clones show the range.

known_object.observer: SPHEREx (geocentric JPL predictions corrected with the spacecraft position from the FITS headers)

scores.definition: Rule-based ranking score in [0, 1]: motion_consistency x snr x (1 - artifact_likelihood). It orders candidates for review. It is not a probability.

explanation.text: Detected in 17 SPHEREx exposures spanning 36.0 hours. It moves 29.2 arcseconds per hour toward position angle 108 degrees. A straight-line fit leaves 2.54 arcseconds of scatter. Its faintest detection has a signal-to-noise ratio of 5.6. Its positions match JPL's prediction for 5193 Tanakawataru (1992 ET) to within 2.8 arcseconds at every epoch.

history.change: linked 17 detections over 5 visits from 2025-12-22 to 2025-12-24
